narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The evangelist Luke; measured, orderly storytelling.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: Jesus of Nazareth, about thirty; calm authority, teaching in parables, warning and consoling.

pharisees.name: Pharisees
pharisees.note: The Pharisees and the scribes together, murmuring that Jesus welcomes sinners; scandalised, disdainful.

1.t: Now the publicans and sinners drew near unto him to hear him.

2.t: And the Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying:
This man receiveth sinners and eateth with them.
2.q: Pharisees and scribes murmur together; given to the canonical pharisees voice rather than a combined id

3.t: And he spoke to them this parable, saying:

4.t: What man of you that hath an hundred sheep, and if he shall lose one of them, doth he not leave the ninety-nine in the desert and go after that which was lost, until he find it?

5.t: And when he hath found it, lay it upon his shoulders, rejoicing?

6.t: And coming home, call together his friends and neighbours, saying to them: Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that was lost?

7.t: I say to you that even so there shall be joy in heaven upon one sinner that doth penance, more than upon ninety-nine just who need not penance.

8.t: Or what woman having ten groats, if she lose one groat, doth not light a candle and sweep the house and seek diligently until she find it?

9.t: And when she hath found it, call together her friends and neighbours, saying: Rejoice with me, because I have found the groat which I had lost.

10.t: So I say to you, there shall be joy before the angels of God upon one sinner doing penance.

11.t: A certain man had two sons.

12.t: And the younger of them said to his father: Father, give me the portion of substance that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his substance.

13.t: And not many days after, the younger son, gathering all together, went abroad into a far country: and there wasted his substance, living riotously.

14.t: And after he had spent all, there came a mighty famine in that country: and he began to be in want.

15.t: And he went and cleaved to one of the citizens of that country. And he sent him into his farm to feed swine.

16.t: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.

17.t: And returning to himself, he said: How many hired servants in my father's house abound with bread, and I here perish with hunger!

18.t: I will arise and will go to my father and say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before thee.

19.t: I am not worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.

20.t: And rising up, he came to his father. And when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion and running to him fell upon his neck and kissed him.

21.t: And the son said to him: Father: I have sinned against heaven and before thee I am not now worthy to be called thy son.

22.t: And the father said to his servants: Bring forth quickly the first robe and put it on him: and put a ring on his hand and shoes on his feet.

23.t: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it: and let us eat and make merry:

24.t: Because this my son was dead and is come to life again, was lost and is found. And they began to be merry.

25.t: Now his elder son was in the field and when he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard music and dancing.

26.t: And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.

27.t: And he said to him: Thy brother is come and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe.

28.t: And he was angry and would not go in. His father therefore coming out began to entreat him.

29.t: And he answering, said to his father: Behold, for so many years do I serve thee and I have never transgressed thy commandment: and yet thou hast never given me a kid to make merry with my friends.

30.t: But as soon as this thy son is come, who hath devoured his substance with harlots, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf.

31.t: But he said to him: Son, thou art always with me; and all I have is thine.

32.t: But it was fit that we should make merry and be glad: for this thy brother was dead and is come to life again; he was lost, and is found.
